items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: I was listening to Sarah Vaughan, who it was just a thrill to listen to her every night. Sarah Vaughan was a very unique person to have in a band of seventeen guys.

ctx.x: think it was a Cable and Nelson or something. But it was a console piano. And I said something to him to the effect of 'Man, there's nothing wrong with the piano. It must be you.' And they said something back to me and left.

So it just happened that these two guys was George Treadwell, the trumpet player that was formerly married to Sarah Vaughan, and Bud Powell was the kid's name. And I didn't see Bud again until after I got to New York, which I'll talk about later, and we really became friends. But Bud must have been about 16 years old then -- he was very young, as I was saying. The band that he was with... It keeps coming to mind that he was with Tiny Bradshaw's band. But when I got to New York a year or so later, he was with…

Anyway, I don't remember whether I mentioned the fact that when we went to Chicago with Trummy, that the tenor saxophone player was a guy whose name was Leo Williams. I don't know whether I mentioned his name. I know I mentioned Tommy Potter and Harry Curtis, the alto saxophone player, Trummy, of course, and Eddie Bert. I don't know if I did mention him or not, but Leo Williams was one of those

items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: So when Sarah asked if she could ride back with me -- fine. She gets in the car with us.

ctx.x: Because Joe has been drinking a little too much. I don't think I want to ride with him." So we said, "Sure!"

In the meanwhile, the theatre that we'd just played in Washington before had a show, and they had a line of chorus girls, who after that engagement were not going to be working for a while. And one of these girls was a friend of Sarah. Sarah asked her to come along with her as an assistant, to help her dress and whatever. Her name was Daisy. I don't remember Daisy's last name. But Daisy was also with Joe. She and Sarah had ridden out there with him.

So when Sarah asked if she could ride back with me -- fine. She gets in the car with us. And we had an expression that we used to use. All bands and groups have things that they say. And when something looks funny or something looks different, we used to just say "There he go" or "There he goes" or something like that. So we were riding down the highway, and we were doing the speed limit, and there's a slight drizzle, rain. All of a sudden, after we had gone about a mile or two, this car whizzed past us, and who…
